energy.overview: Behind-the-meter power is the fastest-moving piece of this layer: Bloom Energy's S&P 500 inclusion and FuelCell Energy's first-ever data-center capacity reservation show fuel cells converting from pilot to real backlog, even as FuelCell's own earnings miss triggered a sharp share drop. Nuclear is bifurcating into near-term wins (DOE closing a $1.9B loan for NextEra's Duane Arnold restart) and longer-dated optionality (SMR and fusion equities swinging hard on sentiment even as underlying construction and PPA milestones, like ENTRA1-TVA and Kairos Power's hardware progress, keep advancing). Grid-scale storage and fusion remain earlier-stage but are attracting outsized private capital, signaling investors expect this bottleneck to persist well past 2026.

cooling.overview: Cooling has moved from a component market to a consolidation battleground: Ecolab, Trane, and Eaton have all closed multi-billion-dollar acquisitions of liquid-cooling specialists in 2026, while Vertiv and Schneider Electric keep raising guidance and rolling out silicon-co-validated reference designs with Nvidia and AMD. Direct-to-chip single-phase cooling has become the default architecture for new AI builds, but two-phase and microfluidic approaches from venture-backed players are still racing to prove out beyond niche deployments as chip TDPs push past 4,000W. The bottleneck is shifting from technology risk to manufacturing and integration capacity, as incumbents scramble to industrialize supply chains fast enough to match GPU shipment growth.

power.overview: Order books and capex commitments across switchgear, transformer, and UPS makers are accelerating faster than physical capacity can be added, with book-to-bills above 2x at several vendors and record backlogs, even as multi-year lead times on high-voltage transformers and medium-voltage switchgear remain the single biggest gating factor on data center energization. Meanwhile, on-board power delivery is entering a genuine architecture race, as Vicor's second-generation vertical power delivery and AmberSemi's backside PowerTile approach both push toward production this year, promising to relieve the 'last inch' bottleneck between rack power and the chip. The net effect is a layer where financial momentum is unambiguously up, but physical throughput is still catching up to demand.

silicon.overview: Memory has become the single tightest constraint in AI infrastructure: HBM, DRAM and NAND are effectively sold out into 2027-2028, prices for even legacy DDR5 and NAND have doubled or more, and Nvidia has now disclosed roughly $267 billion in forward memory commitments through fiscal 2029, forcing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron into record, multi-year capex programs. At the same time TSMC's 2nm ramp is running flat-out and sold out through 2026, while Nvidia's push for custom, co-designed HBM base dies and early processing-in-memory bets hint at the first real cracks in the decades-old logic/memory split.

compute.overview: Custom silicon is scaling faster than the merchant GPU market can supply memory for it: Broadcom and Marvell both raised guidance this cycle on the strength of Google TPU, Anthropic, and Meta ASIC ramps, while AMD's MI450/Helios order book (Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta) is filling out ahead of shipments. The binding constraint has shifted from GPU logic dies to HBM4/CoWoS packaging capacity, which is now so tight it's delaying Nvidia's own consumer GPU roadmap and reshuffling which foundry/design partners (Broadcom, MediaTek, Marvell, now possibly AMD) win each hyperscaler's next TPU generation.

networking.overview: Optical interconnect demand keeps outrunning supply as hyperscalers push through the 800G-to-1.6T transition, forcing capacity expansion at Lumentum and Coherent while co-packaged optics startups like Ayar Labs and Lightmatter cross from prototypes into paid production runs. Switching is being reshaped by Arista's continued share gains over Cisco and by HPE's Juniper integration landing marquee deals like Oracle's gigawatt-scale buildout, even as edge/quantum compute matures with Cerebras now public and SEEQC pushing cryogenic control chips toward commercial supply chains. The picture isn't uniformly bullish: a mid-September equity-offering scare at Corning knocked the whole optics complex down double digits, a reminder that valuations have run well ahead of proven CPO yields.

serversdc.overview: Server OEMs are posting record AI backlogs even as margins swing wildly on component costs, while data center operators are absorbing unprecedented sovereign and private-equity capital to build gigawatt-scale campuses faster than power and permitting can keep pace. Consolidation is accelerating at the top of the market (the $40B Aligned and $4.1B atNorth deals) even as local opposition kills individual projects like QTS's Digital Gateway, showing capital abundance and physical/regulatory constraints are now the defining tension in this layer.

cloud.overview: Hyperscaler cloud capex and backlogs are still compounding rather than plateauing: Oracle, Microsoft, Google Cloud and AWS all posted record remaining performance obligations this quarter even as capital spending keeps getting revised upward and increasingly funded with debt. The constraint has shifted from chips to power and shells, forcing Microsoft into a multi-year, multi-gigawatt buildout plan after losing customers to rivals, while neoclouds like CoreWeave keep growing backlog faster than they can deploy it. The one crack this cycle is financing structure — Nvidia's pullback on vendor-backed revenue-share deals is forcing neoclouds to prove they can fund growth without circular support.

applications.overview: The applications layer is compounding on two fronts at once: frontier labs are racing toward simultaneous mega-IPOs and releasing new flagship models within days of each other, while enterprise and consumer app makers are converting that firepower into real, fast-growing revenue (Salesforce's Agentforce, Harvey, Glean, ServiceNow). The bottleneck is shifting from model capability to monetization proof and distribution, as incumbents like Microsoft, Google, and Salesforce embed multiple third-party frontier models directly into their platforms rather than picking one winner.
